empty.filtered: No domain matches the current search
empty.none: No domains in the registrar ledger yet. Add or sync them on the Domains page.
empty.title: No domains

byDomain.ledgerHint: Business records registered in the host-record ledger (with project/env/owner). Separate from the registrar-side records — present here but absent there means the record does not actually exist yet, or has not been synced.

col.effectiveHint: Only the provider the domain’s NS points at takes effect; edits elsewhere do nothing
col.name: Name

consistency.authorityIncomplete: The “configured but not effective” list is incomplete
consistency.conflictActionKnown: This domain’s NS points at {{authoritative}} ({{ns}}). Only that side’s records take effect; edits anywhere else do nothing.
consistency.conflictActionUnknown: First determine which side this domain’s NS actually points at — only that side takes effect, and records on the other side are dead configuration. (We have not collected this domain’s NS records, so the direction cannot be determined here.)
consistency.conflictHint: These names exist in both Cloudflare and GCP Cloud DNS with different targets. Only the side the NS delegation points to is live; edits on the other side have no effect at all. When chasing "I changed it and nothing happened", first confirm you edited the live side.
consistency.conflictIssue: The same name and type point to different targets on {{a}} and {{b}}.
consistency.conflicts_one: {{count}} domain resolves differently on each side
consistency.conflicts_other: {{count}} domains resolve differently on each side
consistency.ineffective: {{count}} records configured on a provider that is not authoritative
consistency.ineffectiveAction: Either move the records to {{authoritative}}, or switch the NS to {{configured}}. Editing them on this side has no effect at all.
consistency.ineffectiveIssue: These records live on {{configured}}, but the domain’s NS points at {{authoritative}} — only the NS-designated side takes effect.
consistency.oneSidedIssue: Only {{provider}} has records of this type configured.
consistency.scope: Comparison scope (by FQDN; multiple records under one FQDN count once): GCP {{gcp}} · Cloudflare {{cf}} · GoDaddy {{gd}}
consistency.splitNs: {{count}} domains have NS pointing at more than one provider
consistency.splitNsIssue: The NS records point at more than one provider, so which one answers depends on the recursive resolver — that is itself a configuration to fix.

effective.noNote: This domain’s NS points at {{authoritative}} ({{ns}}) — records here have no effect
effective.unknownHint: No NS records collected for this domain, so this cannot be determined. This is not the same as “effective”

empty.partialError: At least one source failed to load, which is why this is empty — it does not mean there are no records. Check the error above, or retry shortly.
empty.reason: Neither source returned data. Either the Cloudflare / GCP account is not connected yet, or the credential lacks DNS read permission. This does not mean these domains have no records.
empty.title: No DNS records retrieved

error.title: DNS records could not be loaded

suspicious.label: Suspicious
suspicious.loopback: Loopback or unspecified address. Resolving here sends visitors back to themselves; nothing external can reach it
suspicious.privateRange: Private range address. On a public domain nothing outside can reach it; on an internal domain this is normal — check the intended use
suspicious.publicResolver: This is a public DNS resolver address (8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1 and friends). Pointing a domain’s A record here means traffic never reaches your service — almost certainly a placeholder or misconfiguration

view.allHint: GoDaddy / Cloudflare / GCP side by side, with the "configured but not effective" check
view.byDomainHint: What records exist under this domain — day-to-day edits happen here
